name: IBPS RRB PO
fullName: IBPS Common Recruitment Process for Regional Rural Banks – Officer Scale I (Assistant Manager)
approxCandidates: ≈6–9 lakh applicants for Officer Scale I (recent cycles, unofficial estimates)
eligibility: Graduate in any discipline; 18–30 years (relaxation for reserved categories); proficiency in the local language of the participating RRB

notification.summary: The CRP RRBs-XV notification was released on 30–31 Aug 2026 with ≈4,256 Officer Scale I vacancies reported (≈13,700 posts across all RRB cadres). Online registration ran from 1 to 21 Sep 2026. The Officer Scale I prelims is scheduled for 21–22 Nov 2026 and the mains for 20 Dec 2026. Dates are from news/education portals; ibps.in could not be reached from the research environment.

pattern.notes: Composite 45-minute paper with no sectional timing; questions are bilingual (Hindi/English). Sectional and overall cut-offs apply and prelims is qualifying only. Mains (200 marks) and an interview (final merit 80:20) follow.

trendAnalysis.summary: RRB PO prelims is a speed test: 80 questions in 45 minutes. Reasoning is easy-to-moderate and puzzle-heavy (4–5 puzzles/seating arrangements, ≈18–22 Qs: floor, box, month, linear with mixed facing, circular), with syllogism, inequality, coding and short miscellaneous questions. Quant is moderate: 2 DI sets (table/bar and caselet, ≈10–12 Qs), quadratic equations, number series (missing and wrong), approximation and arithmetic word problems. Good attempts have usually been 55–65.

resources.notes: IBPS does not publish RRB question papers or answer keys. Official material is the Information Handout (sample questions) and the online practice test released before the exam on ibps.in, plus pre-exam training for eligible candidates. Previous papers are memory-based compilations by coaching portals.

questions.question:
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. B sits second to the left of D. E sits immediately to the left of B. A sits opposite B. C is not an immediate neighbour of D.

Who sits immediately to the right of B?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from A: A, D, F, B, E, C (facing the centre, left = clockwise). B's immediate right (anticlockwise) is F.

questions.question:
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. B sits second to the left of D. E sits immediately to the left of B. A sits opposite B. C is not an immediate neighbour of D.

Who sits opposite D?
questions.explanation: Clockwise: A, D, F, B, E, C. D is in seat 2, so the seat opposite (seat 5) has E.

questions.question:
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. B sits second to the left of D. E sits immediately to the left of B. A sits opposite B. C is not an immediate neighbour of D.

Who are the immediate neighbours of C?
questions.explanation: Clockwise: A, D, F, B, E, C. C sits between E and A.

questions.question:
Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a straight row. Some face north and some face south. R sits at one of the extreme ends and faces south. Only two persons sit between R and S. S faces north, and both immediate neighbours of S face the direction opposite to S. R sits immediately to the right of T. U sits at an extreme end and faces north. T faces the same direction as U. P sits immediately to the left of T.

How many persons face south?
questions.explanation: Left to right (west to east): U (N), Q (S), S (N), P (S), T (N), R (S). Q, P and R face south — three.

questions.question:
Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a straight row. Some face north and some face south. R sits at one of the extreme ends and faces south. Only two persons sit between R and S. S faces north, and both immediate neighbours of S face the direction opposite to S. R sits immediately to the right of T. U sits at an extreme end and faces north. T faces the same direction as U. P sits immediately to the left of T.

Who sits immediately to the right of Q?
questions.explanation: Row (west→east): U (N), Q (S), S (N), P (S), T (N), R (S). Q faces south, so his right is towards the west — U.

questions.question:
Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a straight row. Some face north and some face south. R sits at one of the extreme ends and faces south. Only two persons sit between R and S. S faces north, and both immediate neighbours of S face the direction opposite to S. R sits immediately to the right of T. U sits at an extreme end and faces north. T faces the same direction as U. P sits immediately to the left of T.

Who sits between S and T?
questions.explanation: Row (west→east): U, Q, S, P, T, R. P sits between S and T.

questions.question:
Six persons G, H, I, J, K and L travel in six different months from January to June of the same year (one person per month), each to a different city — Delhi, Pune, Agra, Goa, Ooty and Leh. G travels in a month that has 31 days. H travels in the month immediately before G, and L travels in the month immediately after G. L goes to Delhi. Only one person travels between G and the one who goes to Agra, who travels after G. I travels in June. The one who goes to Goa travels in January and the one who goes to Ooty travels in June. K travels before J. H does not go to Pune. I does not go to Leh. J does not go to Ooty.

Who goes to Agra?
questions.explanation: G must be in March (January leaves no month for H; May would put L in June, which is I's). So H Feb, L Apr (Delhi), Agra in May. K before J gives K Jan (Goa), J May (Agra).

questions.question:
Six persons G, H, I, J, K and L travel in six different months from January to June of the same year (one person per month), each to a different city — Delhi, Pune, Agra, Goa, Ooty and Leh. G travels in a month that has 31 days. H travels in the month immediately before G, and L travels in the month immediately after G. L goes to Delhi. Only one person travels between G and the one who goes to Agra, who travels after G. I travels in June. The one who goes to Goa travels in January and the one who goes to Ooty travels in June. K travels before J. H does not go to Pune. I does not go to Leh. J does not go to Ooty.

In which month does H travel?
questions.explanation: G travels in March, so H (immediately before G) travels in February.

questions.question:
Six persons G, H, I, J, K and L travel in six different months from January to June of the same year (one person per month), each to a different city — Delhi, Pune, Agra, Goa, Ooty and Leh. G travels in a month that has 31 days. H travels in the month immediately before G, and L travels in the month immediately after G. L goes to Delhi. Only one person travels between G and the one who goes to Agra, who travels after G. I travels in June. The one who goes to Goa travels in January and the one who goes to Ooty travels in June. K travels before J. H does not go to Pune. I does not go to Leh. J does not go to Ooty.

How many persons travel between K and L?
questions.explanation: Order: K (Jan, Goa), H (Feb, Leh), G (Mar, Pune), L (Apr, Delhi), J (May, Agra), I (Jun, Ooty). Between K and L: H and G — two.

questions.question:
Seven boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 7 the top). Q is exactly in the middle of the stack. Only two boxes are between Q and P, and P is above Q. N is immediately below R, and R is above Q. Only one box is between M and N. S is above O.

Which box is placed second from the bottom?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: O, S, M, Q, N, R, P. S is second from the bottom.

questions.question:
Seven boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 7 the top). Q is exactly in the middle of the stack. Only two boxes are between Q and P, and P is above Q. N is immediately below R, and R is above Q. Only one box is between M and N. S is above O.

How many boxes are between O and N?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: O, S, M, Q, N, R, P. Between O (1) and N (5) are S, M and Q — three.

questions.question:
Seven boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 7 the top). Q is exactly in the middle of the stack. Only two boxes are between Q and P, and P is above Q. N is immediately below R, and R is above Q. Only one box is between M and N. S is above O.

Which box is placed immediately above Q?
questions.explanation: Q = 4, P = 7; N–R must be 5–6, so N is immediately above Q. M is 3 (two from N), and O, S take 1, 2.

questions.question: Five students A, B, C, D and E scored different marks. B scored more than only two students. D scored more than B but less than A. E scored less than C. Who scored the second lowest marks?
questions.explanation: B is third from the top; A > D > B are the top three, and C > E are below B. Order: A, D, B, C, E — C is second lowest.

questions.question: Four persons P, Q, R and S sit around a square table, one on each side, facing the centre. Q sits to the immediate right of P. S does not sit opposite Q. Who sits to the immediate left of P?
questions.explanation: S is not opposite Q, so S is opposite P, and R is opposite Q. Q is on P's right, so R is on P's left.

questions.question: Five persons V, W, X, Y and Z live on different floors of a five-storey building (floor 1 is the bottom). V lives on an even-numbered floor. W lives immediately above V. X lives on the top floor. Y lives on a floor below Z. Who lives on floor 4?
questions.explanation: X is on 5. V on 4 would put W on 5 (X's), so V = 2 and W = 3. Floors 1 and 4 remain; Y below Z → Y = 1, Z = 4.

questions.question:
Statements: Some boxes are cartons. All cartons are bags.
Conclusions: I. Some boxes are bags. II. Some bags are cartons.
questions.explanation: Boxes that are cartons are bags (I). Since all cartons are bags, some bags are cartons (II). Both follow.

questions.question:
Statements: No car is a bus. All buses are trucks. Some trucks are vans.
Conclusions: I. Some trucks are not cars. II. All vans being cars is a possibility.
questions.explanation: Buses are trucks and no bus is a car, so some trucks are not cars (I). Vans are only linked to trucks; nothing stops all vans from being cars (II is possible). Both follow.

questions.question:
Statement: W > X ≥ Y > Z
Conclusions: I. W > Z  II. Y ≥ W
questions.explanation: W > X ≥ Y > Z gives W > Z; and W > Y, so II is false. Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statements: G ≤ H < I; J > I; K ≥ J
Conclusions: I. K > G  II. H < J
questions.explanation: K ≥ J > I > H ≥ G gives K > G and H < J. Both follow.

questions.question: If 'CLOUD' is written as 'DMPVE' in a code, how is 'RAIN' written?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: R→S, A→B, I→J, N→O = SBJO.

questions.question: In a code, 'WATER' is written as 'XZUDS'. How is 'FIELD' written in that code?
questions.explanation: Letters move +1, −1 alternately: W+1, A−1, T+1, E−1, R+1. FIELD → F+1 = G, I−1 = H, E+1 = F, L−1 = K, D+1 = E = GHFKE.

questions.question: M is the sister of N. N is the son of O. O is the wife of P. Q is the brother of P. How is M related to Q?
questions.explanation: M and N are children of P and O. Q is P's brother, so M is Q's niece.

questions.question: A + B means A is the father of B; A − B means A is the wife of B; A × B means A is the brother of B; A ÷ B means A is the daughter of B. If P × Q + R − S, how is Q related to S?
questions.explanation: Q + R: Q is R's father. R − S: R is S's wife. So Q is the father of S's wife — S's father-in-law.

questions.question: Raj is facing east. He turns 135° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: East → 90° anticlockwise = North → a further 45° = North-West.

questions.question: A is 10 m north of B. C is 6 m east of B. D is 10 m north of C. How far and in which direction is D from A?
In a row of girls, Rita is 13th from the left and Monika is 17th from the right. When they interchange positions, Rita becomes 22nd from the left. How many girls are in the row?
questions.explanation: Rita's new place is Monika's old place: 22nd from the left and 17th from the right. Total = 22 + 17 − 1 = 38.

questions.question: Which letter is 5th to the left of the 9th letter from the right end of the English alphabet (A to Z)?
questions.explanation: 9th from the right = 27 − 9 = 18th letter = R. 5th to its left = 13th letter = M.

questions.question:
Arrangement: B 3 D @ 6 F H 2 # J 8 K % L 5 M
How many letters are immediately preceded by a number and immediately followed by a symbol?
questions.explanation: D (3 D @) and K (8 K %) qualify; F is followed by H and M has nothing after it. Two.

questions.question:
Numbers: 739 482 615 924 368
If the digits of each number are arranged in ascending order within the number, which original number will become the second largest?
questions.explanation: New numbers: 379, 248, 156, 249, 368. In descending order: 379, 368, 249, 248, 156. The second largest, 368, comes from 368.

questions.question:
How is J related to K?
I. J is the brother of L, who is the daughter of K.
II. K is the wife of M, who is the father of J.
options: The data in statement I alone are sufficient, but the data in statement II alone are not
The data in statement II alone are sufficient, but the data in statement I alone are not
The data in either statement I alone or statement II alone are sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are not sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are necessary
questions.explanation: From I: L is K's daughter and J is L's brother, so J is K's son — sufficient. From II: K is J's mother, but J's gender is unknown (son or daughter) — not sufficient.

The table shows the number of farmers (in hundreds) who took crop loans from five RRB branches in 2025 and the percentage of them who were women.
Branch | Farmers | Women %
A | 40 | 30%
B | 55 | 20%
C | 48 | 25%
D | 60 | 35%

How many women farmers took crop loans from branch D?
questions.explanation: 35% of 60 hundred = 21 hundred = 2,100.

questions.explanation: 2025: 20% of 55 = 11 hundred. 2026: 66 × 30% = 19.8 hundred. Increase = 8.8 hundred = 880.

questions.question: 60% of a number is 48 more than 40% of the same number. What is the number?
questions.explanation: 20% of the number = 48 → number = 240.

questions.question: An article marked at ₹2,500 is sold after two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is the selling price?
A dishonest dealer claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a 900 g weight in place of 1 kg. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: He gives 900 g for the price of 1000 g: profit = 100/900 × 100 = 11 1/9%.

questions.question: ₹7,800 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4. What is C's share?
A mother is now three times as old as her daughter. Eight years from now she will be twice as old as her daughter. What is the mother's present age?
questions.explanation: 3D + 8 = 2(D + 8) → D = 8, mother = 24 years.

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they finish a job in 18 days. In how many days can A alone finish it?
questions.explanation: Let B do b per day, A 2b: 3b = 1/18 → b = 1/54, A = 1/27 → 27 days.

questions.question: A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h and the stream flows at 3 km/h. How long will it take to go 36 km downstream and return to the starting point?
questions.explanation: Downstream 36/18 = 2 h; upstream 36/12 = 3 h. Total 5 h.

questions.question: A train crosses a 200 m platform in 20 seconds and a 400 m bridge in 30 seconds. What is the length of the train?
A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at compound interest. In how many years will it become 8 times itself at the same rate?
questions.explanation: 8 = 2³, so it takes 3 × 5 = 15 years.
